title: Frequency density from a frequency
source: Theory IGCSE-20.1 Quick check 1; frequency divided by class width
stem: In a grouped frequency table, the class \({L|int}\lt t\le {U|int}\) has frequency {f|int}. Find the frequency density for this class.

steps.name: W
steps.note: Width is the upper boundary minus the lower boundary.

contexts.note: Includes the original class 10 to 30 with frequency 60, frequency density 3

title: Frequency from the height of a histogram column
source: Theory IGCSE-20.1 Quick check 2; frequency density times class width
stem: On a histogram, the column for the class \({L|int}\lt x\le {U|int}\) has height {fd|int}, where the vertical axis shows frequency density. Find the frequency of this class.

steps.name: W
steps.note: Area of the column represents the frequency.

contexts.note: Includes the original class 5 to 20 with height 6, frequency 90

title: Upper class boundary from frequency and frequency density
source: Theory IGCSE-20.1 Quick check 3; L + f/fd
stem: A class has lower boundary {L|int} and frequency {f|int}. On a histogram, its column has frequency density {fd|int}. Find the upper boundary of the class.

steps.name: W
steps.note: Width is the frequency divided by the frequency density.

steps.name: B
steps.note: Add the width to the lower boundary.

contexts.note: Includes the original lower boundary 20, frequency 45, height 3, upper boundary 35

title: Reading frequencies from a histogram of distances travelled to work

source.note: Stem verbatim from the official QP; marks from the official MS. Question number checked against the QP.

stem:
The histogram shows information about the distance some people travel to work.

(a) Use the histogram to complete the table.

Distance (\(d\) km)Number of people
\(0\lt d\le 5\)
\(5\lt d\le 20\)
\(20\lt d\le 50\)

[3]

(b) The people who travel a distance greater than 35 km to work have a car allowance.

Calculate an estimate of the number of these people who have a car allowance. [1]

steps.name: s1
steps.note: Official MS: B1 for each correct answer: 14.

steps.name: s4
steps.text_tex: (b) From 35 km to 50 km the frequency density is 0.4, so \(0.4\times15=6\).

title: Light and heavy parcels on a histogram

source.note: Stem verbatim from the official QP; marks from the official MS. Question number checked against the QP.

stem:
Kai sorts parcels into two types, light and heavy.

Type of parcelMass (\(m\) kg)
Light\(0\lt m\le 2\)
Heavy\(2\lt m\le 5\)

The histogram shows some information about the number of parcels Kai sorts in one day.

(a) Find the number of light parcels. [1]

(b) There are 102 heavy parcels.

Complete the histogram. [2]

steps.name: s2
steps.text_tex: (b) Frequency density \(=\dfrac{102}{5-2}=34\): draw a column from 2 to 5 with height 34.
steps.note: Official MS: correct column, from 2 to 5 and height 34, 2 marks; or M1 for 102/(5 − 2).

title: Histogram of coconut masses, a probability and an estimated mean

source.note: Stem verbatim from the official QP; marks from the official MS. Question number checked against the QP.

stem:
The histogram shows information about the masses of some coconuts. The masses are classified into four categories \(A\), \(B\), \(C\) and \(D\).

(a) Show that there are 10 coconuts in category \(D\). [1]

(b) Two of the coconuts from those in category \(C\) and category \(D\) are chosen at random.

Find the probability that both are from category \(D\). [3]

(c) Calculate an estimate of the mean mass of the coconuts. [4]

steps.name: s2
steps.text_tex: (b) Category \(C\) has \(170\times0.1=17\) coconuts, so the probability is \(\dfrac{10}{10+17}\times\dfrac{9}{9+17}\).
steps.note: Official MS: M2 for 10/(10 + 170 × 0.1) × 9/(9 + 170 × 0.1) oe, or M1 for 10/(10 + 17) or 9/(10 + 16) or 9/(10 + 17) or 10/(10 + 16) oe seen, or 10/k × 9/(k − 1) oe with k > 10 and an integer, or m/(10 + 17) × (m − 1)/(10 + 16) oe with 0 < m < 27 and an integer.

steps.name: s4
steps.note: Official MS: M1 for frequencies 6, 15, 17 soi.

steps.name: s5
steps.note: Official MS: M1 for midpoints soi (1, 1.175, 1.3, 1.475).

steps.name: s6
steps.note: Official MS: M1 for use of their Σfm ÷ their Σf with m in correct interval including both boundaries.
